answer: At the zenith of network activity, a proof-of-work system can enforce a unique work trail requirement, where each agent must provide a verifiable history of work completed since the last epoch, which is then checked against a random audit sample at the horizon of the current epoch. This approach makes it costly for an attacker to create multiple fake agents, as each one must maintain a consistent and costly work trail that can be verified, effectively creating a deep canyon between legitimate and illegitimate agents.
